title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors

summary: 提出混合专家多模态框架，融合持续元音与朗读语音的声学嵌入及结构化临床、人口学数据识别哮喘，在1218例匹配队列中AUROC为0.83。

abstract: Asthma affects over 260 million people worldwide, yet diagnosis remains dependent on spirometry and specialist assessment, limiting accessibility in primary care and low-resource settings. Vocal biomarkers offer a promising non-invasive alternative, but prior studies have largely focused on acoustic features without integrating clinical context. We present a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework for asthma identification that adaptively combines acoustic embeddings from sustained vowel phonation and reading passage tasks with structured clinical and demographic data. The model was evaluated on a matched cohort of 1218 self-reported asthma cases and healthy controls from the Colive Voice study. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.83 and Brier score of 0.18, outperforming unimodal approaches. Exploratory analysis of the gating mechanism in asthma cases showed that greater respiratory symptom burden was associated with increased weighting of reading-passage modality and reduced weighting of sustained-vowel phonation modality. These findings support the feasibility of voice-based identification of self-reported asthma; however, independent prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.
zh_abstract: 全球有超过2.6亿人受哮喘影响，但其诊断仍依赖肺功能检查和专科评估，限制了其在基层医疗和低资源环境中的可及性。声音生物标志物是一种前景良好的无创替代方法，但既往研究大多聚焦于声学特征，未整合临床背景信息。我们提出了一种用于哮喘识别的多模态专家混合（Mixture-of-Experts）框架，可自适应地将来自持续元音发声和朗读段落任务的声学嵌入与结构化的临床和人口统计学数据相结合。该模型在来自 Colive Voice 研究的1218例自报哮喘病例与健康对照的匹配队列中进行了评估。多模态模型的 AUROC 为0.83，Brier 评分为0.18，优于单模态方法。对哮喘病例中门控机制的探索性分析显示，呼吸道症状负担越重，朗读段落模态的权重越高，而持续元音发声模态的权重越低。这些结果支持基于语音识别自报哮喘的可行性；然而，在临床应用之前仍需进行独立的前瞻性验证。

abstract: Echocardiography assesses the structure and function of the heart. Cardiologists read each study across several standard views and report the findings visible in those views by cardiac structure. AI foundation models can learn to analyze these studies from clinical reports, reducing annotation burden and supporting clinical interpretation. However, existing models are trained by pairing each video with the full clinical report, including structures and findings its view does not show. This mismatch lets a model associate a finding with incidental or spurious signals rather than its visual evidence, which limits accuracy, anatomical grounding and clinical trust. Here we introduce EchoAlign, a vision-language foundation model developed on 2.87 million echocardiographic videos and images from 159 clinical centers. EchoAlign aligns each cardiac structure, video and study with its report text

abstract: [Journal of medical systems] Decision-making in acute and critical care relies on interpretation of heterogeneous information sources under substantial time pressure. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to aid in triage, diagnosis generation, and treatment planning. This scoping review maps the current landscape of LLM-based CDSS in acute and critical care and assesses their readiness for clinical implementation. A PRISMA-ScR-guided search of four databases (January 2026) yielded 62 studies, including 15 medical domain-adapted LLMs. Technology Readiness Levels were assigned across all 62 studies; none has progressed to clinical deployment. Within the medical LLM subgroup, medical LLMs generally outperformed their foundation model counterparts, although the evidence was heterogeneous. An exploratory PROBAST + AI-informed appraisal identified recurring methodological concerns, and thematic synthesis of implementation determinants identified regulatory constraints, workflow integration, and insufficient understanding of human-AI interaction as key barriers. This review highlights priorities for prospective validation using real-world institutional data.
zh_abstract: [Journal of medical systems] 急危重症救治中的决策依赖于在巨大时间压力下对异质性信息来源的解读。大语言模型（LLM）已被提出作为临床决策支持系统（CDSS），用于辅助分诊、生成诊断和制定治疗计划。本范围综述梳理了急危重症领域基于 LLM 的 CDSS 的现状，并评估其临床实施的准备程度。按照 PRISMA-ScR 指引于 2026 年 1 月检索四个数据库，共纳入 62 项研究，其中包括 15 个医学领域适配的 LLM。对全部 62 项研究评定了技术成熟度等级（Technology Readiness Levels）；无一项进入临床部署阶段。在医学 LLM 亚组中，医学 LLM 总体上优于其基础模型对照，但证据存在异质性。一项探索性的、基于 PROBAST + AI 的评价发现了反复出现的方法学问题，对实施决定因素的主题综合则指出，监管限制、工作流程整合以及对人机交互理解不足是主要障碍。本综述强调了使用真实世界机构数据开展前瞻性验证的优先事项。

abstract: [Family practice] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into primary care, yet its adoption is shaped by clinician and patient perceptions, workflow integration, and ethical and system-level considerations. The rapid evolution of generative AI introduces new opportunities and challenges that remain poorly understood. To map and synthesize the literature on AI in primary care, characterize clinician and patient perceptions, identify barriers and facilitators to implementation, and examine the implications of generative AI. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR scoping review of studies published from 2020 onward. Six databases were searched, supplemented by gray literature and hand-searching. Data were synthesized descriptively and thematically. Thirty-two studies were included. Family physicians reported benefits including improved workflow efficiency, documentation support, and clinical decision-making, alongside concerns regarding trust, accuracy, workflow integration, and medico-legal accountability. Patients generally supported AI when clinician oversight was maintained. Generative AI, particularly ambient documentation systems, improved workflow but introduced risks including hallucinated outputs, authorship ambiguity, and increased verification burden. Across studies, trust, workflow integration, and preservation of relational care consistently emerged as key determinants of successful AI adoption. AI has considerable potential to enhance primary care, but successful adoption depends less on technological capability than on strengthening trust, integrating into clinical workflows, and preserving relational care. As generative AI becomes embedded in practice, education, governance, and oversight will be essential to ensure safe, equitable, and patient-centered care.
zh_abstract: [Family practice] 人工智能（AI）正越来越多地融入基层医疗，但其应用受到临床医生和患者的认知、工作流程整合以及伦理和系统层面因素的影响。生成式 AI 的快速发展带来了新的机遇和挑战，而这些仍未被充分理解。本研究旨在梳理并综合基层医疗中 AI 的相关文献，描述临床医生和患者的认知，识别实施的障碍和促进因素，并探讨生成式 AI 的影响。我们按照 PRISMA-ScR 开展了一项范围综述，纳入 2020 年起发表的研究。检索了六个数据库，并辅以灰色文献和手工检索。数据采用描述性和主题方法进行综合。共纳入 32 项研究。家庭医生报告的获益包括工作流程效率提高、文书记录支持和临床决策改善，同时也担忧信任、准确性、工作流程整合以及医疗法律责任问题。当保持临床医生监督时，患者总体上支持 AI。生成式 AI，尤其是环境式文书记录系统，改善了工作流程，但也带来风险，包括幻觉性输出、作者归属不明确以及核查负担增加。在各项研究中，信任、工作流程整合和维护关系型照护始终是成功采用 AI 的关键决定因素。AI 具有显著增强基层医疗的潜力，但成功采用更多取决于加强信任、融入临床工作流程和维护关系型照护，而非技术能力本身。随着生成式 AI 融入临床实践，教育、治理和监督对于确保安全、公平和以患者为中心的照护至关重要。

abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play essential roles in transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization, yet predicting their functional properties from sequence remains challenging because informative signals span both local motifs and long-range base pairing across kilobase-scale transcripts. Current RNA foundation models are restricted to short sequences and existing lncRNA prediction models narrowly focus on isolated tasks, leaving a dedicated foundation model notably absent. Here we present LncRFM, a dedicated lncRNA foundation model, supported by the LncCorpus pretraining data and the LncBench evaluation suite, which stand for a systematic framework to decode lncRNAs. For foundation model pretraining, we develop a hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder trained with a structure-guided masking strategy to effectively capture both local sequence patterns and long-range contexts. For pretraining data, we contribute over 9.6 million lncRNA sequences to assemble LncCorpus, a pretraining corpus of 24.7 million sequences. For benchmarking evaluation, we construct a comprehensive benchmark, LncBench, comprising 15 datasets and totaling over 1,010,000 sequences across 10 prediction tasks: six core lncRNA functional and annotation tasks and four structural and regulatory RNA assay tasks. Evaluated against seven RNA foundation models under a unified frozen-encoder protocol, our LncRFM achieves the state-of-the-art primary-metric scores on 11 of the 13 datasets that allow downstream adaptation. On two external generalization benchmarks evaluated without further adaptation, LncRFM matches the best structure-specialized baseline in F1 (0.141) and achieves the highest AUROC (0.962) on lncRNA contact prediction, while maintaining competitive cross-species coding-potential transfer (F1 of 0.374) under severe multi-kingdom domain shift. To benefit the scientific community, we make all datasets, source code, and pretrained models publicly available.
zh_abstract: 长链非编码 RNA（lncRNA）在转录调控和染色质组织中发挥重要作用，但由于有效信号既包括局部基序，也包括跨越千碱基尺度转录本的长程碱基配对，从序列预测其功能特性仍具挑战。目前的 RNA 基础模型仅限于短序列，现有 lncRNA 预测模型又仅狭隘地聚焦于孤立任务，因此尚缺乏专门的基础模型。在此，我们提出 LncRFM，一个专门的 lncRNA 基础模型，并由 LncCorpus 预训练数据和 LncBench 评估套件提供支持，它们共同构成解码 lncRNA 的系统框架。在基础模型预训练方面，我们开发了一种混合双向状态空间编码器，并采用结构引导的掩码策略进行训练，以有效捕获局部序列模式和长程上下文。在预训练数据方面，我们贡献了超过 960 万条 lncRNA 序列，构建了包含 2,470 万条序列的预训练语料库 LncCorpus。在基准评估方面，我们构建了综合基准 LncBench，包含 15 个数据集，共计超过 1,010,000 条序列，涉及 10 项预测任务：6 项核心 lncRNA 功能与注释任务和 4 项结构与调控 RNA 实验任务。在统一的冻结编码器方案下与七个 RNA 基础模型比较，LncRFM 在允许下游适配的 13 个数据集中的 11 个上取得了最先进的主要指标得分。在两个无需进一步适配即可评估的外部泛化基准上，LncRFM 在 F1 上与最佳结构专用基线相当（0.141），并在 lncRNA 接触预测上取得最高 AUROC（0.962），同时在严重的多界域偏移下仍保持有竞争力的跨物种编码潜能迁移表现（F1 为 0.374）。为造福科学界，我们公开了所有数据集、源代码和预训练模型。

The goal is often to maximize potency while keeping other properties within the ranges required for a viable therapeutic candidate. Compound prioritization places different demands on computational methods as drug discovery progresses from hit identification through hit-to-lead and lead optimization, with changing computational budgets and increasing amounts of on-target experimental data. We introduce Ruby, a Robust Universal Binding affinitY predictor that uses intermediate representations from the structural foundation model Pearl without requiring an explicit binding pose for every compound. Ruby is trained on proprietary data plus GenesisPotency-2026, an audited public-source potency training dataset released for academic and commercial use under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license with row-level provenance

abstract: [Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care] Adolescent mental health remains a topic of concern in the United States and worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the youth mental health crisis, which began nearly a decade earlier. The ongoing shortage of mental health professionals, including therapists and child and adolescent psychiatrists, means many adolescents who require mental health treatment do not receive it. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated promise in the field of adolescent mental health, including in screening, detection and risk prediction, intervention and treatment, clinical decision support and workflow augmentation, and in the training of future mental health professionals. However, the study of AI tools in the mental health space remains in its infancy, and most are not yet ready for routine use in clinical practice. Furthermore, the potential risks of AI and its use in adolescent mental health treatment are significant and must be addressed prior to widespread use. Health care professionals, adolescents, and their caregivers need to develop AI literacy to use the technology safely and responsibly. Additionally, AI governance and legal frameworks are necessary to ensure that AI technology use is safe, equitable and ethical for all users. At the present time, AI technology should serve a supportive and complementary role to human-delivered adolescent mental health care.

abstract: [International journal of technology assessment in health care] To identify the topics and outcome measures used to evaluate patient-related aspects of digital health technologies (DHTs), and to propose a comprehensive framework to guide evidence requirements for their assessment in health technology assessments (HTA). A scoping review was conducted to identify the topics and outcome measures for the evaluation of patient-related aspects of DHTs. Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched. Extracted data included article identifiers, type of tool used for evaluation, topics, outcome measures, intended purpose of the DHT, and Artificial Intelligence capability according to the European Digital Health Technology Assessment (EDiHTA) taxonomy. Descriptive analyses were undertaken to summarize methods, topics, and outcome measures. A thematic analysis of measurement items was then conducted to address conceptual overlap. Finally, outcome measures were mapped to the Warwick Patient Experiences Framework (WaPEF). 336 articles were included in this review. Patient-related aspects were evaluated using qualitative methods (n = 164), non-validated tools (n = 127), and validated tools (n = 119). From the validated tools, twelve topics and 155 outcome measures were identified. After resolving conceptual overlaps, these were refined to nine topics and twenty-eight outcome measures. Most outcome measures mapped to WaPEF; however, two topics, caregiver burden and satisfaction, were not fully captured by WaPEF. This review proposes a framework for evaluating patient-related aspects in HTA of DHTs, comprising nine topics and twenty-eight outcome measures. By focusing on outcome measures, the framework improves conceptual clarity and supports a more systematic, and patient-centered approach to DHT evaluation.

abstract: [Investigative ophthalmology & visual science] Glaucoma is increasingly recognized not as a uniform pressure-defined optic neuropathy, but rather as a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder driven by interacting genetic, metabolic, mechanical, vascular, inflammatory, and environmental factors. Although genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics have each yielded important insights, no single omics layer can fully capture the multilevel architecture underlying differences in disease susceptibility, progression, and treatment response. Multi-omics therefore offers a more integrated framework for linking inherited risk, gene regulation, cellular states, protein activity, metabolic vulnerability, and imaging phenotypes to clinically relevant outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in multi-omics research in glaucoma, spanning genomics, epigenomics and transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics, microbiome studies, and emerging approaches such as spatial omics, single-cell multi-omics, radiomics, and exposomics. We further discuss how cross-layer integration, network analysis, Mendelian randomization, imaging genomics, and multimodal artificial intelligence are helping to define convergent pathogenic pathways and clinically relevant molecular subtypes. Particular attention is given to four major pathological axes: extracellular matrix-mechanical stress, mitochondrial-metabolic dysfunction, immune-microbiome dysregulation, and exposure-vascular burden. Despite ongoing challenges in standardization, cohort size, validation, and interpretability, multi-omics is shifting glaucoma research toward mechanism-based stratification and deployable precision care.

abstract: [HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery] Unregulated peptides like BPC-157 are heavily marketed for musculoskeletal recovery despite the lack of U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval and minimal evidence from human trials. With peptide content widely promoted on social media, patients increasingly consult artificial intelligence (AI) tools to evaluate claims regarding the efficacy of these products. We sought to compare the accuracy, completeness, and readability of AI-generated information on unregulated peptides for musculoskeletal recovery across dedicated AI tools and social-media-embedded assistants. We performed a cross-sectional content analysis study of AI outputs in response to 4 standardized questions about unapproved peptide use. Seven dedicated AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, OpenEvidence, Elicit, Undermind, and Consensus.ai) and 4 social-media assistants (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and X) were queried in May 2026. Readability was assessed using a composite of 4 grade-level formulas. Two evidence-anchored questions were scored by 3 blinded reviewers (2 orthopedic surgeons and 1 immunopathologist) using the validated Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI) instrument (6-30) for the 7 dedicated AI tools but not for the 4 social media assistants. Mean QAMAI score across the dedicated tools was 21.6/30 (good), ranging from 17.8 (Undermind, fair) to 25.3 (Claude, very good). Among dedicated tools, pooled QAMAI domain scores were highest for accuracy (4.0/5) and lowest for completeness (3.3/5). Among social-media assistants, X and Facebook were accurate, TikTok was mixed, and Instagram (Meta AI) spread misinformation, claiming BPC-157 accelerates recovery and endorsing post-surgical use. All 11 tools produced outputs at the college level (mean grade: 13.9), above the sixth-to-eighth-grade target for patient materials, with no correlation between quality and readability. Our analysis suggests that AI tools cannot substitute for clinical counseling on unregulated peptides. The accuracy subscore was generally strong, but completeness and readability remained poor. Medical societies should partner with AI developers to standardize evidence-anchored responses and prevent patient harm. Level IV: observational content analysis study.
zh_abstract: [HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery] 尽管缺乏美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）的批准，且人体试验证据极少，BPC-157 等未受监管的肽类产品仍被大力推销用于肌肉骨骼恢复。随着肽类内容在社交媒体上被广泛推广，患者越来越多地求助人工智能（AI）工具来评估这些产品的功效宣称。我们旨在比较专用 AI 工具与嵌入社交媒体的 AI 助手所生成的、关于未受监管肽类用于肌肉骨骼恢复的信息在准确性、完整性和可读性方面的差异。我们开展了一项横断面内容分析研究，分析 AI 对 4 个关于未获批肽类使用的标准化问题的回答。于 2026 年 5 月对 7 个专用 AI 工具（ChatGPT、Gemini、Claude、OpenEvidence、Elicit、Undermind 和 Consensus.ai）及 4 个社交媒体助手（Instagram、Facebook、TikTok 和 X）进行了查询。可读性采用 4 种年级水平公式的综合指标进行评估。其中 2 个以证据为基础的问题，由 3 名盲法评审者（2 名骨科医生和 1 名免疫病理学家）使用经验证的医疗人工智能质量评估（QAMAI）量表（6-30 分）对 7 个专用 AI 工具进行评分，4 个社交媒体助手未进行评分。各专用工具的 QAMAI 平均得分为 21.6/30（良好），范围从 17.8（Undermind，一般）到 25.3（Claude，非常好）。在专用工具中，QAMAI 各领域合并得分以准确性最高（4.0/5），完整性最低（3.3/5）。在社交媒体助手中，X 和 Facebook 的回答准确，TikTok 的回答好坏参半，而 Instagram（Meta AI）传播了错误信息，声称 BPC-157 可加速恢复并认可术后使用。全部 11 个工具生成的内容均为大学水平（平均年级：13.9），高于患者材料六至八年级的目标水平，且质量与可读性之间无相关性。我们的分析提示，对于未受监管的肽类，AI 工具无法替代临床咨询。准确性子评分总体较强，但完整性和可读性仍然较差。医学学会应与 AI 开发者合作，使以证据为基础的回答标准化，以防止对患者造成伤害。证据等级 IV：观察性内容分析研究。

abstract: [JMIR nursing] Large language model (LLM)-powered virtual patient systems are gaining popularity in nursing education but also face persistent challenges, such as hallucinations and role inconsistency. This paper reports the model architecture design, technical considerations, implementation challenges, and evaluation of an LLM-powered AI-assisted simulated-patient system integrated into a nursing triage simulation game. The system integrated a Unity-based game client, with GPT-4o hosted through Microsoft AI Foundry to support real-time simulated-patient dialogue in Traditional Chinese using Cantonese syntax. This developmental study comprised exploratory model selection, formative student feedback-informed enhancement from Version 1 to Version 2, development-stage script-fidelity evaluation, and evaluation of system usability and the Net Promoter Score in 2 tutorial cohorts of nursing students. Key technical contributions include a layered hallucination mitigation architecture that combines grounded prompt inclusion, few-shot conversational exemplars, negative role constraints, and calibrated model parameters. In the predefined script-fidelity evaluation, script-inconsistent responses occurred in 78 of 125 (62.4%) Version 1 outputs and 21 of 125 (16.8%) Version 2 outputs-an absolute difference of 45.6 percentage points. The implementation process also addresses stateless API memory management, cloud-based safety filter calibration for domain-specific clinical prompts, and prompt engineering strategies to prevent role drift and hidden scenario information leakage. GPT-4o was selected as the production model through exploratory development testing that considered script consistency, Cantonese-language suitability, response latency, technical reliability, deployment feasibility, cost considerations, and Unity integration compatibility; 45 of 50 (90%) assessed GPT-4o responses were rated fully script-consistent. This study demonstrates the development and real-world tutorial deployment of a Cantonese-language, LLM-powered simulated-patient system for nursing triage education. Integrating formative student feedback with structured technical debugging enabled iterative refinement of dialogue fidelity, role consistency, protected-information handling, and game interaction functions. The resulting Version 2 system provides a practical, contextually tailored approach to supporting scalable simulated-patient dialogue in nursing education.

abstract: [Frontiers in public health] Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and related systems are being investigated for nursing and nursing-adjacent work, but inconsistent terminology and heterogeneous evaluations obscure their operational capabilities and clinical relevance. This review examined the relationship between reported agentic behavior, evaluation in nursing practice, retained decision authority, and evidence concerning patient benefit, workload, and accountability. We conducted a scoping review informed by JBI guidance and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. We searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation and linked-report searching. Among 28 reports, 13 satisfied all criteria, four were indeterminate, and 11 lacked at least one criterion. Only two qualifying reports evaluated live nurse-AI workflows. Nursing participation ranged from clinical work to education, co-design, output rating, and outcome assessment, and did not uniformly represent runtime control. Patient-facing clinical workflows retained professional decision authority; robotics evaluations involved neither nurses nor patients. Outcomes principally concerned technical performance, communication, usability, or component-specific efficiency. The evidence did not establish autonomous nursing practice, sustained patient benefit, or reduced complete-episode nursing workload. No empirical evaluation of accountability or redress following AI-related error was identified. Operational qualification, clinical benefit, and accountable use require separate evaluation. Future studies should assess the complete human-AI pathway, including verification, correction, escalation, patient outcomes, and responses to failure. Comparative designs should isolate agentic mechanisms from additional computation, information access, and workflow redesign. A proposed post hoc, unvalidated heuristic links allocated function, decision authority, assurance, and accountability/redress. Interpretation is limited by absent prospective registration, unquantified agreement before consensus, related reports, and the absence of formal risk-of-bias assessment. Agentic capability alone does not establish clinical readiness. Expanding AI-enabled functions requires evidence of meaningful benefit, effective human control, and accountability arrangements proportionate to the consequences of system actions.
zh_abstract: [Frontiers in public health] 智能体人工智能（AI）及相关系统正被用于护理及护理相关工作的研究，但术语不一致和评估方式异质，使其实际操作能力及临床相关性难以明晰。本综述考察了所报告的智能体行为、护理实践中的评估、保留的决策权，以及关于患者获益、工作负荷和问责的证据之间的关系。我们参照 JBI 指南开展了范围综述，并按 PRISMA-ScR 进行报告。我们检索了 PubMed、Embase、CINAHL、Scopus 和 Web of Science，并辅以引文检索和关联报告检索。在 28 篇报告中，13 篇满足全部标准，4 篇无法判定，11 篇至少缺少一项标准。仅有 2 篇符合条件的报告评估了真实的护士-AI 工作流程。护理人员的参与范围从临床工作到教育、共同设计、输出结果评分和结局评估，并不一致地代表运行时控制。面向患者的临床工作流程保留了专业人员的决策权；机器人评估既未涉及护士也未涉及患者。结局主要涉及技术性能、沟通、可用性或特定组件的效率。现有证据未能证实自主护理实践、持续的患者获益或完整诊疗过程中护理工作负荷的减少。未发现对 AI 相关差错后的问责或救济进行的实证评估。操作资格、临床获益和可问责使用需要分别评估。未来研究应评估完整的人机路径，包括核验、纠正、升级处理、患者结局以及对失败的应对。比较性设计应将智能体机制与额外的计算、信息获取和工作流程重新设计区分开来。本文提出了一种事后的、未经验证的启发式框架，将分配的功能、决策权、保障措施与问责/救济联系起来。对结果的解释受到以下限制：缺乏前瞻性注册、达成共识前的一致性未量化、存在相关报告，以及未进行正式的偏倚风险评估。仅凭智能体能力并不能证明其已具备临床应用条件。扩大 AI 赋能的功能，需要有证据证明其具有切实获益、有效的人为控制，以及与系统行为后果相称的问责安排。

abstract: [Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications] Immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining is frequently used to resolve diagnostically ambiguous prostate cancer biopsy findings on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. However, PIN-4 IHC is typically performed on adjacent tissue sections, limiting direct spatial comparison between the H&E morphology that indicated the need for IHC and the corresponding immunophenotypic signal. A paired, registered H&E/PIN-4 dataset was constructed from routine clinical prostate biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs), and a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) was trained to synthesize PIN-4 staining patterns directly from native H&E image patches. The final dataset comprised 172 paired WSIs from 93 patients and 27,298 registered 1024 × 1024 patch pairs, spanning adenocarcinoma-positive and benign cases with representation across age, race, and ethnicity groups. The model was evaluated on an independent held-out test set of 1,814 patch pairs from 17 WSIs, achieving a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 21.88 dB, structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.667, Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.684, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.417. Qualitative review by a board-certified pathologist demonstrated that generated images captured diagnostically relevant PIN-4 staining patterns, including AMACR/racemase expression and basal-cell-associated staining, while preserving spatial correspondence with the source H&E morphology. Synthesis quality varied across morphologically complex regions, including high-grade carcinoma and intraductal carcinoma. These results support the feasibility of supervised computational PIN-4 staining from routinely acquired brightfield H&E prostate biopsy images. The approach enables direct interpretation of predicted PIN-4 marker patterns in the context of the source prostate H&E architecture, addressing a current spatial limitation of conventional adjacent-section IHC.
zh_abstract: [机器学习与应用国际会议论文集] 免疫组织化学（IHC）染色常用于解决苏木精-伊红（H&E）染色组织上前列腺癌活检诊断不明确的发现。然而，PIN-4 IHC通常在相邻组织切片上进行，限制了提示需要进行IHC的H&E形态与相应免疫表型信号之间的直接空间比较。我们利用常规临床前列腺活检全切片图像（WSI）构建了配对、配准的H&E/PIN-4数据集，并训练条件生成对抗网络（cGAN），直接从原生H&E图像块合成PIN-4染色模式。最终数据集包含来自93例患者的172张配对WSI和27,298对配准的1024 × 1024图像块，涵盖腺癌阳性和良性病例，并涵盖不同年龄、种族和族裔群体。模型在来自17张WSI的1,814对图像块的独立保留测试集上进行评估，平均峰值信噪比（PSNR）为21.88 dB，结构相似性指数（SSIM）为0.667，Pearson相关系数（PCC）为0.684，学习感知图像块相似度（LPIPS）为0.417。经委员会认证的病理医师定性评阅表明，生成图像捕捉到了具有诊断相关性的PIN-4染色模式，包括AMACR/消旋酶表达和基底细胞相关染色，同时保持与源H&E形态的空间对应。在形态复杂的区域（包括高级别癌和导管内癌）中，合成质量存在差异。这些结果支持从常规获取的明场H&E前列腺活检图像进行有监督计算式PIN-4染色的可行性。该方法可在源前列腺H&E结构的背景下直接解读预测的PIN-4标志物模式，解决了传统相邻切片IHC目前存在的空间局限。

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] This chapter explores the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented wearable technology in dynamic health monitoring across diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation. Innovations include real-time cardiovascular disease detection, AI-driven continuous glucose monitoring for diabetes, and neurological disorder tracking using flexible electroencephalograph (EEG) sensors. Therapeutic advances feature smart drug-delivery patches responsive to biomarkers, remote intervention systems, and surgical tools like augmented reality (AR) navigation. Rehabilitation breakthroughs encompass wearables for motor recovery, cardiopulmonary optimization, and neurorehabilitation using brain-computer interfaces. Future progress hinges on multifunctional hardware, federated learning for privacy, explainable AI, and standardized regulations.

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Multi-omics integration amalgamates genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic layers to provide a systems-level portrait of multifaceted diseases such as cancer. However, its practical application faces constraints posed by challenges including elevated dimensionality, diverse data types, and prevalent missing values. This review delivers a structured summary of recent advances in machine-learning-driven integration of multi-omics datasets, with a specific emphasis on the potential of this field for translational cancer research. First, we discuss the importance of multi-omics integration. Next, we provide an overview of key machine learning methodologies, including high-dimensional variable selection techniques (e.g., knockoff filters for controlling the false discovery rate), deep learning models (for survival prediction and classification), and generative models (e.g., diffusion models and variational autoencoders for data augmentation and missing data imputation). These approaches demonstrate high accuracy in cancer subtype classification, biomarker discovery, prognosis evaluation, and personalized therapy. For example, they achieve over 85% accuracy in triple-negative breast cancer subtype analysis. We also cover the contributions of single-cell multi-omics technologies (e.g., SHARE-seq and SNARE-seq) and emerging databases (e.g., scImmOmics and scCancerExplorer) to enhancing data resolution. While challenges remain in terms of interpretability and computational efficiency, integrating explainable AI and multimodal learning shows promise in accelerating clinical translation. This review seeks to equip researchers with a systematic methodological roadmap and demonstrate its practical utility in precision medicine via exemplar case studies.
zh_abstract: [分子生物学方法（Clifton, N.J.）] 多组学整合融合了基因组、转录组、表观基因组和蛋白质组等层面的数据，可为癌症等多因素疾病提供系统层面的全景图像。然而，其实际应用受到高维度、数据类型多样以及缺失值普遍存在等挑战的制约。本综述对机器学习驱动的多组学数据集整合的最新进展作了结构化总结，并特别强调该领域在转化性癌症研究中的潜力。首先，我们讨论多组学整合的重要性。接着，我们概述关键的机器学习方法，包括高维变量选择技术（例如用于控制错误发现率的 knockoff 过滤器）、深度学习模型（用于生存预测和分类）以及生成模型（例如用于数据增强和缺失数据填补的扩散模型和变分自编码器）。这些方法在癌症亚型分类、生物标志物发现、预后评估和个体化治疗方面表现出较高的准确性。例如，它们在三阴性乳腺癌亚型分析中的准确率超过 85%。我们还介绍了单细胞多组学技术（例如 SHARE-seq 和 SNARE-seq）以及新兴数据库（例如 scImmOmics 和 scCancerExplorer）在提高数据分辨率方面的贡献。尽管在可解释性和计算效率方面仍存在挑战，但整合可解释人工智能与多模态学习有望加速临床转化。本综述旨在为研究者提供系统的方法学路线图，并通过示例案例研究展示其在精准医学中的实际应用价值。

abstract: [Biomarker research] Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents

abstract: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. Masking reasoning and diagnosis, the same 4B model scores sufficiency from objective evidence via prior-debiased probabilities over five ordered levels. abstract: PathOPEN is a histopathology dataset for visual question answering. abstract: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.

abstract: [International journal of nanomedicine] Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability. abstract: [Current opinion in ophthalmology] Recent advances are extending optical coherence tomography (OCT)'s role beyond conventional structural metrics. This review summarizes recent developments in macular OCT, OCT angiography (OCTA), artificial intelligence (AI), and portable/home-based OCT. Macular ganglion-cell measures (ganglion-cell-inner plexiform layer, ganglion cell complex) increasingly complement retinal nerve fiber layer assessment, offering greater diagnostic/prognostic value in advanced glaucoma, myopia, and certain glaucoma subtypes. OCTA is emerging as a complementary vascular biomarker; peripapillary vessel density shows the most consistent link to progression, with early evidence that vascular changes may precede detectable structural or functional decline. Deep learning models increasingly use raw or multimodal imaging rather than summary parameters; foundation and multimodal architectures (e.g., RETFound-based) show strong diagnostic performance and improved generalizability across demographics and disease severity. However, AI-based progression prediction remains less robust than cross-sectional diagnosis, especially under external validation. Portable/home-based OCT may extend monitoring beyond the clinic, though clinical utility remains investigational. The field is moving toward multimodal, longitudinal, AI-supported glaucoma assessment integrating structural, vascular, and functional biomarkers rather than interpreting them in isolation. Key priorities for translation include standardized acquisition and analysis across devices, large and diverse external validation cohorts, interpretable models, and evidence that AI and remote imaging improve clinically meaningful outcomes. These developments should make OCT increasingly central to earlier detection and individualized monitoring of glaucoma, but none currently replace established structural and functional assessment or clinical judgment.

abstract: [Chronic diseases and translational medicine] Public omics repositories and multi-omics technologies have substantially expanded the molecular characterization of chronic human diseases by enabling large-scale analyses across diverse biological and clinical contexts. However, in neurological disorders, translating omics-derived associations into mechanistic insight and clinical relevance remains challenging due to the dynamic and multiscale nature of brain function. Gene set-based analytical approaches effectively identify enriched molecular patterns, but are limited in capturing temporal dynamics, network-level interactions, and physiological state dependence that define neural systems. This conceptual methodological review synthesizes foundational infrastructure papers, methodological evaluations, and translational neuroscience literature to critically examine the application of public omics resources in human neurophysiology, focusing on the interpretive gap between molecular-level associations and functional brain processes. We examine major public omics infrastructures, widely used gene set analysis frameworks, the principal strategies for multi-omics integration, and the challenge of batch effects in public data reuse, highlighting both their analytical strengths and structural limitations. Core neurophysiological principles, including synaptic transmission, network dynamics, plasticity, and homeostatic regulation, are discussed to clarify why direct inference from static molecular profiles to brain function is inherently constrained. Clinical illustrations from epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and migraine demonstrate how chronic neurological disorders emerge from context-dependent neural dynamics that are not readily reducible to gene set-level summaries. Finally, we outline future directions for integrating artificial intelligence with public omics resources, emphasizing physiology-informed modeling, explainable AI, and ethical considerations to support more interpretable and translational precision health strategies in chronic neurological disease.

abstract: [Clinical genitourinary cancer] Agreement of large language models with multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) decisions in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer is unknown. First-line MDT recommendations (2020-2023) were compared with those of GPT-4o configured with European Association of Urology guidelines and institutional procedures. Recommendations for androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), systemic intensification, and radiotherapy were classified as not recommended, optional, or recommended, and summarized as a normalized consensus score; agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa (κ). Scoring weights were tested in sensitivity analyses; non-consensus cases were reviewed post hoc by 2 urologists. Full consensus occurred in 14.1%, partial consensus in 50.0%, and no consensus in 35.9%; full consensus did not exceed 37% under any alternative scoring scheme. Binary agreement was 88.5% for ADT (κ -0.05, prevalence effect), 56.4% for radiotherapy (κ 0.05), and 71.8% for systemic intensification (κ 0.25). Agreement with documented MDT decisions was low and mainly reflected recommendation strength, particularly for radiotherapy. abstract: [Systematic reviews] Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) imposes a substantial burden on patients and healthcare systems. Although traditional risk assessment tools exist, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) may offer improved prediction. This systematic review aims to evaluate the performance of ML and DL algorithms for predicting AECOPD risk. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were systematically searched from 1 January 2021 to 6 May 2026. Studies that developed or validated ML and DL models for predicting AECOPD risk were included. Methodological quality, risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI, and reporting quality was assessed using the TRIPOD + AI. Because of substantial heterogeneity, we synthesised model performance descriptively. Thirteen studies were included, of which only two performed external validation. Overall, reported AUC values ranged widely from 0.661 to 0.9721. By outcome type, AUC values for AECOPD risk prediction ranged from 0.668 to 0.9721, whereas those for AECOPD‑related hospitalisation ranged from 0.661 to 0.885. Similarly, by prediction windows, short‑term prediction achieved AUCs of 0.668‑0.972, compared with 0.661‑0.884 for long‑term prediction. However, PROBAST + AI revealed high methodological quality concerns and risk of bias in all 13 studies, and TRIPOD + AI showed suboptimal reporting transparency with an overall completeness rate of 54.3%. Limited evidence indicates that models for any AECOPD may outperform those for hospitalisation, and that models with shorter prediction windows may show higher AUCs, although this association could be confounded by small sample sizes and potential patient-level leakage. These findings provide valuable direction for future model development and validation, although the current evidence base is constrained by methodological quality concerns, risk of bias and suboptimal reporting transparency. abstract: [Nature and science of sleep] Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains one of the most prevalent yet underdiagnosed chronic disorders worldwide, with persistent challenges in timely diagnosis and long-term adherence to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) have emerged as promising digital health technologies that address complementary aspects of OSA management. AI has demonstrated strong diagnostic performance under controlled conditions in automated OSA detection, severity classification, and physiological signal analysis, whereas AR is being tested as a way to improve CPAP mask fitting, patient education, and treatment engagement. However, the integration of these technologies has received little attention in either the scientific literature or clinical practice. This commentary highlights the emerging convergence of AI and AR as a novel paradigm for OSA diagnosis, treatment initiation, and self-management. Current evidence indicates that AI-driven AR applications are beginning to appear at the commercial level, yet robust OSA-specific clinical evidence remains limited. Potential applications include AR-guided home diagnostic setup, AI-assisted CPAP mask fitting and desensitization, and personalized AR-based coaching to support long-term treatment adherence. We also discuss key barriers to implementation, including the limited evidence base, algorithmic bias from training data that underrepresent some populations, the privacy of sleep and facial data, the digital divide that affects older and low-income patients, regulatory pathways, and uncertainties regarding clinical integration. Finally, we propose a research agenda, guided by implementation science frameworks, focused on feasibility, usability, patient acceptability, and comparative effectiveness against existing educational and telemedicine approaches, to determine whether AI-driven AR represents a meaningful advance in OSA care. Establishing this evidence base will be essential for translating this emerging technological convergence into routine clinical practice.

abstract: [Frontiers in public health] The evolution of medical epistemology from the unassailable authority of eminence to the empirical rigour of evidence has prepared the healthcare system for its most profound transformation yet, intelligence-based medicine. Driven by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), this emerging era offers unprecedented capabilities to process complex health data and personalise patient care within high-stakes environments like emergency departments. However, this paradigm shift simultaneously introduces a critical risk of modernised, digital dogma, manifesting as algorithmic paternalism. If AI systems are deployed without rigorous oversight, they threaten to silently amplify historical biases, diagnostic inaccuracies, and outdated clinical heuristics, trading the unquestioned authority of historical figures for the presumed infallibility of machines. To safeguard care in emergency departments, AI must not operate unchecked. Adapting existing Learning Health System frameworks offers a pragmatic solution to govern AI integration. By embedding these computational technologies within continuous, self-correcting clinical ecosystems, departments can enforce robust data hygiene and rigorously audit data provenance. An essential component of this approach is separating objective safety surveillance and adverse event reporting from the algorithm's internal learning mechanisms to detect epistemic drift and automation bias. Ultimately, the successful and safe integration of intelligence-based medicine depends on an unwavering commitment to transparent governance. When computational power is harnessed as a regulated, transparent tool within an LHS, AI can actively dismantle entrenched clinical dogma, ensuring future care is anchored in dynamic, validated evidence rather than perpetuating the medical errors propagated by eminence from the past.

Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis. Guided by Rodgers' evolutionary method, the literature was analyzed to determine how AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses has been used and conceptualized. Defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, and related concepts were extracted, compared, and synthesized. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. Search terms focused on nurses, nursing students, health workers, artificial intelligence literacy, algorithmic literacy, AI competence, AI readiness, and generative AI literacy. Articles published between January 2020 and June 2026 were screened. Twenty-eight articles were included in the final concept analysis. Four defining attributes were identified: conceptual understanding of AI-mediated nursing contexts; critical interpretation and risk recognition of algorithmic outputs; clinical integration and human oversight of AI recommendations; and ethical governance awareness grounded in professional accountability. Antecedents included AI education and training, digital or informatics foundations, prior AI exposure, individual readiness, organizational support, faculty preparedness, and governance environments. Consequences included improved learning outcomes, critical thinking, AI adoption and readiness, patient safety awareness, human-AI collaboration, and professional innovation.
